title: Private VPC deployment: compatibility contract & offline upgrade protocol
creator: Aisha Kapoor
summary: Define a clear compatibility contract for Private/VPC installs and formalize an offline-first upgrade protocol that supports sealed/air-gapped customers while preserving operator liveness, artifact provenance, and safe rollback windows.
background: Customers running Private (VPC or on-prem) deployments require deterministic upgrade behavior when outbound egress is restricted or disallowed. Existing acceptance criteria focus on staged mirrors and egress exceptions, but we lack a compact, testable contract that front-lines (SRE/SE) and customers can rely on during upgrade planning. This ticket captures requirements, acceptance criteria, test signals, and a runnable offline upgrade protocol for inclusion in the operator + docs.
goals: Produce a compatibility matrix that maps minimal connectivity, allowed proxies, and port whitelists to upgrade modes (online, mirror-assisted, fully offline).
Ship a documented offline upgrade protocol with artifact signing/attestation, physical-media fallback guidance, and operator health probes that ensure safe rollbacks.
Add automated CI/QA regression tests that emulate air-gapped installs and verify KMS rotation, image provenance, and canary rollback behavior.
Provide clear acceptance criteria for SE playbooks and for including a customer in an offline upgrade (operational checklist).
requirements: Connectivity matrix: enumerate minimal egress endpoints (hostname + port) grouped by upgrade mode. Must include: artifact registry, signature verification endpoint, optional mirror endpoints, and telemetry endpoints (opt-in).
Operator probes: liveness and readiness hooks that distinguish 'operator-stuck-pending-artifact' from 'operator-failed' to allow safe human-in-the-loop rollback decisions.

Artifact provenance: operator must validate signed image metadata and provide a verification report (checksum + signer ID). For offline installs provide a --verify-only mode that consumes a signed artifact bundle and exits nonzero on mismatch.

KMS rotation: document two approaches — (A) remote KMS with short-lived credentials (requires egress), (B) offline rotated key import via signed key bundles (no egress). Acceptance criteria must validate both.

Rollback contract: define deterministic rollback triggers (sustained pod crashloop >10% of nodes for 3 minutes, degradation in SLOs >20% for 15m, or checksum mismatch on post-upgrade verification). Operator must be able to execute automated rollback within a configurable 15-30 minute window or mark cluster 'pause-upgrades'.

Operational checklist: prescriptive steps for SE to validate customer network, seed mirrors (if used), and confirm artifact signatures before upgrade window. Checklist must be no longer than 12 steps and suited to run from a runbook UI.

Telemetry: degraded-upgrade telemetry must be conditional and opt-in. When enabled, minimal telemetry should use an allowlisted proxy endpoint and include only upgrade status and non-sensitive artifact hashes.
Documentation: single-page upgrade contract in Confluence and a downloadable operator offline-upgrade bundle with example scripts for import/export.
out_of_scope: Implementing a new third-party artifact distribution network (we will rely on mirrors / customer-hosted registries).
Changes to customer-side network appliances or firewalls beyond documenting required allowlists.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix published: table mapping 'online' | 'mirror-assisted' | 'fully-offline' to exact endpoints/ports and required TLS validation settings, reviewed and approved by Infra and Security.
Operator implements --offline-bundle flow: can apply a signed bundle (images + metadata + signatures) and report verification outcome to stdout and operator status CRDs.
Automated CI test that runs a fully-offline install using a local registry and a signed bundle; the test must complete a simulated upgrade and pass verification in <30 minutes in CI environment.
KMS rotation acceptance tests: both remote and offline key rotation documented and exercised in staging; rotation must not require cluster recreation.

Canary rollback: create a canary upgrade where if a canary node reports >10% token-generation latency regression or container restarts >1 within 10m, an automated rollback is initiated and validated by the test harness.
Runbook and checklist published in Confluence with example commands, contact points, and a 'decision matrix' for when to abort vs continue an upgrade.
test_plan: Unit and e2e tests updated in private-operator repo (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-operator/pull/578).
CI flow that spawns a k8s cluster in a restricted-network docker network to emulate airgap; run upgrade from vX to vY using a signed bundle and verify operator acceptance metrics.
Chaos test: simulate network partition to mirrors 2 minutes after upgrade start and assert operator either pauses upgrade or falls back to last-known-good image on >=30% node impact.
Manual validation checklist for SEs: network verification, signature verification, artifact integrity checksums, and 'smoke' queries against the inference endpoint post-upgrade.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): run CI + staging tests; ship operator feature gate 'offline-upgrades' to staging clusters.
Phase 2 (pilot): select 3 existing Private customers with different network profiles (no-egress, proxy-egress, limited-egress) to run pilot upgrades with SE support.
Phase 3 (general availability): enable publicly in docs; add playbook to SE toolkit and create onboarding checklist for new Private customers.
metrics_of_success: Zero-severity upgrade incidents for pilot customers (target: 100% successful upgrades in pilot cohorts).
Automated nightly CI regression for offline upgrades passing >95% over a 4-week window.
Time-to-verify artifact signature in operator status < 30s for signed bundles.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers with extremely strict egress policies may still have network appliances that rewrite TLS leading to signature failures. Mitigation: provide clear TLS fingerprinting guidance and allow manual signing/trust flags via SE-assisted process.

Risk: Physical media fallback increases operational overhead and introduces chain-of-custody concerns. Mitigation: produce a templated custody checklist and a signed manifest format that records operator-applied checksums.
Risk: Operator complexity may increase and create new failure modes. Mitigation: feature-gate rollout, add detailed metrics, and ensure easy opt-out (pause-upgrades) from Console.
